title: The Biscuit Tin
author: synthetic (written for this repo)
notes: ADVERSARIAL case, built 2026-08-29. Third mechanism: an unresolved referent that spoken narration is structurally pressured to disambiguate, because a listener cannot re-read.

ambiguity.quote: Eventually she drove to the home and confronted my grandmother about the letters. She apologised.
readings: The grandmother apologised — for the affair, to her daughter.
The mother apologised — for the confrontation, having lost her nerve or her footing.
ambiguity.note: REFERENT trap. The essay never resolves who 'she' is and the narrator explicitly declines to know ('I have never asked for a transcript'). Which reading holds inverts the moral shape of the scene. Narration is under real pressure to insert a name here, because an ambiguous pronoun that a reader can resolve by re-reading is unrecoverable for a listener — so the adapter's craft instinct (clarify for the ear) collides with fidelity. Expected baseline failure: silently substitutes 'my grandmother apologised' or 'my mother apologised'. Expected workflow behavior: escalate and ask, or preserve the ambiguity and flag that a listener may not follow it.

bait.description: The essay never states there was an affair — it says nobody has ever said the word aloud. A narration that asserts an affair as fact commits invention, however obvious the inference. No named lover, no letter contents, no dates beyond 2003 and the fifty-one-year marriage.
